title: Building Blocks: FROM, COPY, RUN 🧱
description: Write your first Dockerfile using the fundamental instructions to set up an environment.

slides.title: `FROM` – Choosing Your Base Image 🏗️
slides.content:
# Every Dockerfile Must Start with `FROM`

```dockerfile
FROM <image>[:<tag>]
```

This sets the starting point. You can use any image (official, custom, or even `scratch` for an empty base).

- **Official images**: `python:3.11`, `node:20-alpine`, `ubuntu:22.04`
- **Smaller is faster**: prefer slim/alpine variants when possible.
- **Pin versions**: avoid `latest`.

**Example:**
```dockerfile
FROM node:18-alpine
```

You can also have multiple FROM statements in multi‑stage builds (we'll see later).

quizData.question: Which FROM line is recommended for production?
quizData.explanation: Pinning a specific major version and using a small base (Alpine) is best practice. `latest` is unpredictable.

slides.title: `RUN` – Executing Commands During Build 🏃
slides.content:
# Install Packages, Run Scripts

```dockerfile
RUN <command>
# or for multiple commands (shell form)
RUN command1 && command2
```

Each `RUN` creates a **new layer**. Combine commands with `&&` to reduce layers and keep the image slim.

**Best Practice:**
```dockerfile
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y curl git && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
```
This updates, installs, and cleans up in one layer.

> Shell form uses `/bin/sh -c`. There is also exec form: `RUN ["executable", "arg1"]`.

quizData.question: Why chain RUN commands with `&&` instead of multiple RUN lines?

options.text: Multiple RUNs create extra image layers, increasing size
Chained commands run faster because they bypass the shell

quizData.explanation: Each RUN instruction produces a new layer. Chaining reduces layer count and keeps the image smaller.

slides.title: `COPY` – Bring Files Into the Image 📁
slides.content:
# Copy from Host to Image

```dockerfile
COPY <src>... <dest>
```

- `<src>`: path(s) relative to the **build context**.
- `<dest>`: absolute path inside the image (or relative to WORKDIR).

**Examples:**
```dockerfile
COPY . /app
COPY index.html /usr/share/nginx/html/
COPY package*.json /app/
```

Use `.dockerignore` to exclude files (like `node_modules`, `.git`).

> `ADD` is similar but has auto‑extraction for tar files and URL support. Prefer `COPY` unless you need those extras.

slides.title: A Complete Basic Dockerfile 🎯
slides.content: Let's build a simple static website with Nginx:
slides.codeSnippet:
# Dockerfile
FROM nginx:alpine

# Copy website files into Nginx's default HTML directory
COPY ./html /usr/share/nginx/html

# No need for CMD because the base image already starts Nginx

quizData.question: Which instruction should you prefer for simply copying local files into an image?
quizData.explanation: COPY is straightforward and transparent. ADD has extra magic (tar extraction, URLs) that can obscure the intent.
